case_title.quote: N PARAMESWARAN UNNI v. G KANNAN AND ANOTHER

number_of_accused.reason: Only the first respondent is the accused.

accused_gender.quote: borrowed Rs. 64,000/- oil 13-10-1990 from the appellant/complainant. ... his bank
accused_gender.reason: The judgment uses 'his' for the first respondent, so gender is indicated as male; 'Not stated' is slightly off.

victim_gender.reason: Cheque dishonour is a victimless offence; no victim is identified.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: first respondent/accused borrowed Rs. 64,000/- oil 13-10-1990 from the appellant/complainant

offence_category.reason: Cheque dishonour is not among the listed categories, so 'Other' fits.

statutory_provisions.quote: Section 138 r/w 142 of N.I. Act is attracted

evidence_type.quote: documentary evidence adduced on behalf of the parties

trial_court_outcome.quote: convicted and sentenced the first respondent to undergo simple imprisonment of three months

high_court_outcome.quote: allowed the revision by reversing the concurrent findings of the two Courts below

final_outcome.quote: we set aside the impugned judgment of the High Court.
final_outcome.reason: Conviction restored; the in-lieu payment is arguably a modification, but 'convicted' fits better because conviction is upheld.

offence_finally_established.quote: Section 138 r/w 142 of N.I. Act is attracted

imprisonment_type.quote: conviction and sentence of three months awarded by the Ld. Trial Court ... shall stand restored
imprisonment_type.reason: Sentence is replaced by deposit, but three months imprisonment is restored on default; 'none' is debatable.

imprisonment_years.quote: conviction and sentence of three months ... shall stand restored
imprisonment_years.reason: Three months sentence stands on default of deposit, so null is incomplete.

fine_rs.quote: deposit the said amount of Rs. 2,00,000/-
fine_rs.reason: Deposit is compensation in lieu of imprisonment, not a fine.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Remove the court-related content; the summary should avoid unsupported details.
neutral_facts.quote: Appellant got issued a legal notice on 12-04-199 l to the first respondent, which was returned with postal endorsement
neutral_facts.reason: It says the notice was received back on 25 April by the advocate, which is supported. But the dishonour for 'insufficiency of funds' is only alleged, and it describes the accused's cheque origin loosely; also it omits the complaint. Mostly fine but includes the 'alleged' claim as fact.

offence_severity.quote: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both

motive.quote: first respondent failed to return the borrowed amount Rs. 64,000/-

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the first notice sent by appellant on 12-04-1991 was effective and notice was deemed to have been served

bail_history.quote: bail granted to the first respondent shall stand cancelled
bail_history.reason: Accurately reflects the reference to bail.

legal_representation.quote: C. K. Sasi, Manu Krishnan G., Abraham Mathews (for P. V. Dinesh), Advs. for the Respondents.

investigation_status.quote: On 23.05.1991 appellant lodged a private complaint

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Second notice issued beyond 15 days was treated by the High Court as a lapse, which the SC held irrelevant
procedural_irregularity.quote: the second notice has no relevance at all
procedural_irregularity.reason: The alleged notice-limitation lapse was considered, though rejected.

appeal_history.quote: we set aside the impugned judgment of the High Court.

prosecution_argument.reason: Arguments not separately recorded; inferred position reasonable.

legal_principle_applied.quote: once notice is sent by registered post by correctly addressing to the drawer of the cheque, the service of notice is deemed to have been effected

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Jagdish Singh v. Natthu Singh, ( 1992) I SCC 647

sentencing_rationale.quote: In view of the undertaking given by the learned counsel

other_sentence_order.quote: Rs.1,30,000/-( one lakh thirty thousand) shall be paid to the appellant as compensation
